extracted.intended_audience: NIH communications staff and other federal health communicators (writers of web content, fact sheets, brochures, newsletters, press releases, and promotional materials)
extracted.subtask_description: NIH-specific style guidance for creating web content, fact sheets, brochures, newsletters, press releases, and other promotional or public-facing materials; emphasizes alignment with AP, HHS, plain-language, accessibility, and subject-specific language guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended use / scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIH Style Guide is intended for use in writing web content, fact sheets, brochures, newsletters, and other promotional materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not intended for scientific publications; use AMA, NLM, and other scientific styles for manuscripts. Use this guide when preparing public-facing communications and promotional materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary reliance on AP Stylebook for news/media
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH follows the Associated Press (AP) Stylebook for news releases and other media products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open and read the links to the AP Stylebook found in many entries; the AP guidance for that topic is primary and anything included here is in addition to AP or providing additional context. Whenever NIH diverges from HHS or AP’s guidance, the divergence is explicitly stated in this guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fallback to HHS and AP for uncovered items
rubrics_metrics.description: For items not covered by this guide, please refer to HHS’ style guide and AP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the NIH guide lacks direction on a topic, consult the HHS style guide and AP for authoritative guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not for scientific publications
rubrics_metrics.description: This style guide is not intended for scientific publications, which typically follow the American Medical Association, the National Library of Medicine, and other styles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use AMA, NLM, or journal-specific styles for manuscripts, citations, and other scientific publication formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Plain Writing Act of 2010 (Public Law 111-274) aims to improve clarity and simplicity in government communication. The law requires federal agencies to use clear language that the public can understand and use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply plain-language principles (clarity, brevity, active voice, organization for readers) in public-facing NIH communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Science, Health, and the Public Trust guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides guidelines on communicating science and health research to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be sure to reference the Understanding Clinical Studies page when writing about studies and clinical trials; follow the Science, Health, and the Public Trust best practices when presenting research findings to lay audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Spanish Style Guide
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides best practices for communications professionals who translate and write Spanish health, science, or clinical research materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the NIH Spanish Style Guide for Spanish-language translations and original Spanish materials to ensure appropriate terminology, tone, and cultural considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Executive Secretariat Style Guide
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the Executive Secretariat Style Guide for procedural and formatting requirements when drafting controlled or official correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: PubMed / PubMed Central / NLM style for citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides information on the National Library of Medicine (NLM) style for journal abbreviations, date formats, page numbers, and authors, as well as other styles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing citations, references, or materials that draw on biomedical literature, follow NLM conventions for abbreviations, dates, page numbers, and author formatting. Note that inclusion in PubMed/PMC does not imply endorsement by NLM/NIH.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 508 / accessibility requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Section508 Guide to Accessible Web Design and Development provides guidance for developers, designers, and content creators to ensure that federal websites and digital products meet the Revised 508 Standards, part of Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure content, design, and code meet Revised 508 accessibility standards (e.g., alt text, contrast, keyboard accessibility, semantic structure) when publishing web and digital materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Person-first and Destigmatizing Language
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See NIH Style Guide section for specific recommendations on using person-first constructions and language that avoids stigmatizing people or conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alcohol and Substance Use
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See NIH Style Guide section for specific recommended terminology, framing, and destigmatizing language around alcohol and substance use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disabilities
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See NIH Style Guide section for guidance on respectful, person-first, and non-stigmatizing language regarding disabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Autism
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See NIH Style Guide section for autism-specific language preferences and recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obesity and People with Higher Weight
rubrics_metrics.description: Obesity and People with Higher Weight
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See NIH Style Guide section for guidance on terminology and framing that avoids stigma and respects people with higher weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See NIH Style Guide section for recommended language and considerations when referring to people of different ages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Race and National Origin
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See NIH Style Guide section for guidance on appropriate, respectful, and precise terminology for race, ethnicity, and national origin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grammar and Punctuation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See NIH Style Guide section for NIH-specific advice and any departures or clarifications relative to AP or other style manuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerals
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See NIH Style Guide section for rules on when to spell out numbers versus using numerals, and any NIH-specific conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure and Formatting
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See NIH Style Guide section for recommendations on headings, paragraphing, lists, metadata, and other formatting conventions for public-facing materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix: Biomedical Definitions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the appendix for definitions of biomedical terms used in NIH communications to ensure consistency and accuracy.
